title: Wreckage
question: Today, can the narrator find any life left in his home at Maybury?
light: morning sun from the east, deep black shadows
palette: scorched grey, crimson red weed, pale gold dawn, mahogany brown, black mourning wool

hill_crest.described: The trodden yellow clay crest of an earthwork rampart fills the lower third of the picture, heaped mounds of London clay with thin threads of grey smoke rising behind them. Below the crest the green waves of Regent's Park roll out across the middle of the picture, and beyond them a vast field of slate roofs and chimneys glints white where the sun strikes. Small and clear on the skyline stand the dome of the Albert Hall, the Westminster towers in haze, and the dark dome of St Paul's with a gaping cavity in its west side. Low sunrise light falls in from the east at the left of the frame, throwing long black shadows of the clay mounds toward the right across the trodden crest.
hill_crest.landmark: the dark dome of St Paul's with the cavity in its west side
hill_crest.landmark_size: small, a tenth of the frame tall
hill_crest.route: from the clay crest at the bottom edge out over the park to the skyline
hill_crest.geometry: The clay rampart crest runs along the BOTTOM edge and fills the lower third, each mound a fifth of the frame wide. The Regent's Park trees fill the centre band, a quarter of the frame's height. The roofscape fills the upper half up to the horizon on the top third line. The dome of St Paul's stands at the LEFT third on the skyline, a tenth of the frame tall, with the rising sun beside it near the LEFT edge. The Westminster towers stand at the RIGHT third in haze, smaller still, and pale gold sky fills the TOP edge.
hill_crest.ambience: dawn birdsong, rooks calling over the hill, a light wind across the clay, distant church bells

sickroom.described: A first-floor back bedroom of a St John's Wood villa at night. Against the far wall stands a brass-railed bedstead with a rumpled white counterpane and two pillows. Beside it at the left stands a marble-topped washstand holding a white jug, a basin and folded cloths, with a cane chair in front of it. Above the bed hangs a framed engraving of a cathedral. At the right a tall sash window carries drawn lace and heavy green rep curtains on a brass pole. A shaded oil lamp on the washstand throws warm amber light from the left across the counterpane, and the far right corner sinks into deep black shadow. A Turkey carpet covers the dark stained boards.
sickroom.route: from the panelled door at the near edge to the bedside at the far wall
sickroom.geometry: The brass bedstead stands across the CENTRE, its foot rail on the bottom third line and its headboard against the far wall on the top third line, the bed half the frame wide. The washstand and the shaded lamp stand at the LEFT third, a third of the frame tall. The curtained sash window fills the RIGHT edge from the top edge down to the bottom third. The cathedral engraving hangs above the headboard at the TOP edge centre, a tenth of the frame wide. The Turkey carpet fills the BOTTOM edge.
sickroom.ambience: a ticking marble clock, the lamp flame hissing, church bells ringing far across London

line_repair.described: A railway line outside a Surrey station on a bright summer morning, under hasty repair. Fresh pale sleepers and temporary rails run on raw grey ballast from the foreground to the far distance. Stacks of new sleepers and piles of twisted old rail lie along the left side of the track, and a wagon loaded with rails stands on a siding beside them. Blackened shells of brick houses stand along the embankment on the right, their roofs reduced to charred rafters, their walls grimy with black powder. Clumps of crimson red weed choke the ditches on both sides. Morning sun falls from the east at the left of the frame, laying long black shadows of the sleeper stacks across the ballast.
line_repair.landmark: the stacks of new sleepers beside the rail wagon
line_repair.landmark_size: medium, a quarter of the frame tall
line_repair.route: along the track from the near ballast to the vanishing point at the far end
line_repair.geometry: The double track runs from the BOTTOM edge centre, half the frame wide, to a vanishing point at the CENTRE on the top third line. The stacked sleepers and the rail wagon stand at the LEFT third, a quarter of the frame tall. The blackened house shells stand along the RIGHT edge, the nearest a third of the frame tall and the farthest a tenth. Crimson weed fills the ditches in both lower corners. Pale haze and clear sky fill the TOP edge above the far end of the line.
line_repair.crowd: hundreds of clerks, shopmen and navvies laying sleepers side by side, a distant mass of small figures at the far end of the track
line_repair.ambience: picks ringing on rails, shovels biting ballast, a locomotive's steam far down the line, larks over the fields

maybury_road.described: A gravel country road runs away from a small station toward Maybury in daylight. Dark pine woods rise along the right side of the road, and a five-bar field gate stands on the left, opening onto a flat meadow. Tangled crimson fronds of a fleshy red weed choke the ditches and verges on both sides, neck-high in places. In the fronds at the left verge lies a warped and broken dog cart on its side, one wheel lifted, with the whitened, gnawed bones of a horse scattered among the stems. A line of telegraph poles runs alongside the road. Morning sun falls from the left over the meadow, throwing the black shadows of the pines across the dry sandy road.
maybury_road.landmark: the warped dog cart in the red weed
maybury_road.landmark_size: medium, a quarter of the frame wide
maybury_road.route: from the station forecourt at the near edge along the sandy road into the pine wood at the far end
maybury_road.geometry: The sandy road enters at the BOTTOM edge centre, half the frame wide, and narrows to the CENTRE on the top third line. The pine wood fills the RIGHT third from the bottom edge to the top edge. The field gate stands at the LEFT third, a fifth of the frame tall, with the meadow behind it. The broken dog cart lies in the weed at the LEFT edge on the bottom third, a quarter of the frame wide, its lifted wheel a tenth of the frame tall. The telegraph poles step along the right verge, shrinking toward the far end.
maybury_road.ambience: wind in the pines, larks over the meadow, telegraph wires humming, gravel under boots

villa_front.described: A detached two-storey red-brick villa on a sloping suburban road in daylight. A grey slate roof carries two tall brick chimney stacks. White sash windows stand open, grey with dust along their sills, and a canted bay window stands left of the black front door under a small tiled porch. The front door hangs forced and ajar on its hinges, its lock splintered. A knee-high brick front wall with a wrought-iron gate runs along the road, and behind it stand trampled laurels and smashed privet. A gravel road climbs to the right in the foreground. Tall beech trees stand downhill at the left, and crimson weed fronds edge the foot of the fence. Daylight falls from the left behind the beeches, laying their black shadows across the gravel.
villa_front.landmark: the forced black front door under the tiled porch
villa_front.landmark_size: medium, a fifth of the frame tall
villa_front.route: from the gravel road at the bottom edge through the iron gate up the path to the front door
villa_front.geometry: The villa fills the CENTRE, two thirds of the frame wide, its roof ridge on the top third line and its chimneys reaching toward the TOP edge. The black front door stands right of centre, a fifth of the frame tall, under the porch. The bay window stands at the LEFT third. The front wall and iron gate run along the bottom third, the gate at the centre a tenth of the frame tall. The beech trees fill the LEFT edge; the gravel road crosses the BOTTOM edge and climbs off at the RIGHT edge.
villa_front.ambience: wind in the beeches, the forced door creaking on its hinges, a blackbird in the laurels, a far train whistle

dining_room.described: A late-Victorian dining room in daylight, seen from inside toward a pair of glazed French windows standing open. Faded crimson velvet curtains and grey-dusted lace hang to either side of the open doors. Beyond them two stone steps lead down to a sunlit overgrown lawn with broken rose trees, trampled shrubs and tall beech trees. In the foreground stands the corner of a mahogany table under grey dust, holding a plate of decayed mutton, a heel of blackened bread and a brown beer bottle lying on its side, a balloon-back chair pushed askew beside it. Dark red damask wallpaper covers the walls above a walnut dado. Daylight pours in through the open French windows from the far side, throwing the black shadows of the window bars across the Turkey carpet toward the camera.
dining_room.route: from the table corner in the foreground to the open French windows and the stone steps beyond
dining_room.geometry: The open French windows fill the CENTRE, half the frame wide, from the top third down to the bottom third, the bright lawn framed inside them. The crimson curtains hang at the LEFT third and the RIGHT third, each a sixth of the frame wide. The dusty table corner fills the BOTTOM edge at the RIGHT, a third of the frame wide, the beer bottle and the plate on it each a tenth of the frame. The stone steps sit at the foot of the window opening, and the beech trees fill the top of the opening near the TOP edge.
dining_room.ambience: a mantel clock ticking, the curtains stirring in the breeze, blackbirds on the lawn, wind in the beeches

shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the narrator's wet face, widening to show the clay crest and the roofs of London across the whole shot; tears run down the narrator's cheeks as he lifts his face to the sky; his shoulders shake with sobbing.
shots.camera: On the clay crest a yard in front of him, at his chest height, a 50mm lens; the sunrise light comes from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's wet face at the RIGHT third, his head a third of the frame's height, tears bright on his cheeks. Behind him at the LEFT third the dark dome of St Paul's sits small on the skyline, and the yellow clay mounds fill the BOTTOM edge under a pale gold sky.

source: I stood weeping and praising God upon the summit of Primrose Hill
And then I forget.
shots.turn: a man who saved his own memory of the day -> a man whose memory breaks
shots.why: Opens on the last thing he remembers; the strangest part of his story begins in a blank, and shows a man broken by relief.

shots.why: While he forgets, the news he found flies from London to every city; the world rejoices without him, and he is shown as one wanderer among many.

shots.frame: Wide on the red-brick villa at Maybury in daylight, the narrator (grey eyes, straw boater with a black band) small at the iron gate, the forced black front door ajar under the tiled porch.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the road to the tall beech trees, travelling two strides, across the whole shot; the narrator faces the house from the iron gate; the black door swings open a hand's breadth in the wind.
shots.camera: On the far verge of the gravel road at a man's height, twenty yards from the house, a 35mm lens; the daylight comes from the LEFT behind the beeches.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the tall beech trees at the LEFT edge, their black shadows lying across the gravel road. The villa fills the CENTRE beyond them, the forced black door right of centre a fifth of the frame tall, and the narrator stands at the iron gate on the BOTTOM third, a tenth of the frame tall.
shots.end: The forced black front door stands at the CENTRE under the tiled porch, swung a hand's breadth wider, the narrator a small figure at the iron gate on the BOTTOM third facing it, the bay window at the LEFT third and the chimneys reaching the TOP edge.

shots.why: The slam is the only answer at his own door; inside, his unfinished paper and their muddy footsteps wait as he left them.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I remember that whole day clearly, until I stood weeping and praising God on Primrose Hill.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Then I forget.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Others found the dead Martians before me. The news flew to Paris, and all England rang bells.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The Last Man Left Alive! Hurrah! The Last Man Left Alive!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Kind strangers sheltered me. Gently, they told me Leatherhead was gone, every soul in it.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I stayed four days.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Then the craving to see my home won. I left them in tears, and took a free train.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I sat alone and watched the ruins flow past.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Just past the terminus, every house was a blackened shell.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Every little stream lay choked with red weed, like butcher's meat and pickled cabbage.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: It hurt to look at.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The line was broken before Woking, so I left the train at Byfleet and walked toward Maybury.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: In the weed I found the dog cart, warped and broken, and the horse's gnawed white bones.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I stood a long time.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A man at a cottage door called my name, and I walked on.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I looked at my house with a flash of hope. It faded at once.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The door was forced.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: It slammed.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Upstairs, under its selenite weight, my unfinished paper still lay on the desk, broken mid-sentence.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The mutton lay rotting. My home was desolate.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A voice said no one had escaped but me. I turned.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: And there on the step, amazed and afraid as I was, stood my cousin and my wife.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: My wife, white and tearless.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I made a step across the room, toward the open window.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: She gave a faint cry, and at last I believed.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: She stood on the threshold, one hand at her throat.

lines.speaker: narrators_wife
lines.text: I came. I knew... I knew...
